title: Chromatin preparation and ChIP from Drosophila brain and discs tissues
protocol: Dissect third instar larvae for 20 minutes in ice-cold PBS, removing gut and fat body but leaving carcass attached.

Fix carcasses immediately after dissection for 20 min at room temperature in cross-linking solution (1.8% formaldehyde, 50 mM Hepes pH 8, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 100 mM NaCl), changing the solution 3-4 times.
Stop fixation by washing for 3 min in PBS/0.01% Triton X-100/125 mM glycine, repeating the wash 3-4 times.

Wash fixed carcasses for 10 min in wash A (10 mM Hepes pH 7.6, 10 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 0.25% Triton X-100), followed by a 10 min wash in wash B (10 mM Hepes pH 7.6, 200 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 0.01% Triton X-100), changing the solution 3-4 times.
Store carcasses at 4°C in wash B (maximal overnight).
Dissect brain and disc tissues off fixed carcasses in wash B and pool approximately 400 to 800 complexes for one chromatin sample.
Lysate brain disc complexes in 0.5 ml RIPA buffer.
Sonicate the lysate twice for 2 minutes using a tip sonicator set to power output: 20, pulser: 60.
Transfer the material to a Covaris sonication tube and add porcelain beads if desired.
Sonicate the material three times for 10 minutes in a Covaris machine at maximum settings.
Remove insoluble material by centrifugation at 4°C for 20 min at 16000 g.
Dilute soluble chromatin with RIPA buffer without N-Laurylsarcosine to achieve desired concentration per brain disc complex.
Aliquot diluted chromatin and quick-freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen aliquots at -80°C to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

Use 35-100 μl of diluted chromatin to quantify by qPCR after reversal of cross-links \(treated from RNase step onwards as described below), to obtain an estimate of the chromatin concentration (input DNA).
Prepare 50 % bead suspension by equilibrating 0.1 g Protein A Sepharose CL-4B beads in 1 ml RIPA (with all protease inhibitors), incubate at 4 °C for 1 h.
Spin at 4 °C for 10 min at 16000 g and re-suspend in 500 μl RIPA.
Pre-clear chromatin by adding 50 %v/v beads suspension and incubate at 4 °C for 1 h (rotating).
Incubate the pre-cleared chromatin with specific antibodies (anti-L(3)mbt1211-1477aa and anti-dSfmbt531-980aa) at 4 °C over night (12-16 h).
Incubate antibody-chromatin complexes with 40 ml of 50% v/v beads suspension at 4°C for 3 hours.
Wash the complex at 4°C, 10 minutes with 1 ml RIPA buffer, repeat five times.
Wash the complex once more at 4°C, 10 minutes with 1 ml LiCl solution.
Wash the complex twice at 4°C, 10 minutes each time with 1 ml TE buffer.
Remove supernatant by centrifuging at 4°C for 30 seconds at 16,000 g after each wash.
Resuspend beads in 100 μl TE buffer.
Incubate the suspension with 50 μg/ml RNase at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Quickly spin down samples to separate supernatant and pellets.
Incubate samples with 0.5 mg/ml proteinase K at 55°C for 1 hour.
Reverse cross-links by incubating samples at 65°C (shaking at 350 rpm if using a shaking heat block) for 6 hours or overnight.
Perform phenol/chloroform extraction using Phase-Lock heavy gel tubes following manufacturer's instructions.
Transfer sample to 2 ml Phase-Lock tube and add one volume of Phenol-Chloroform, shake for 5 minutes at room temperature, then spin at 13,200 rpm for 5-10 minutes.
Transfer upper phase to a fresh 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
To precipitate DNA, add 1/10 volume of 3 M NaOAc pH 5.2 and 2.5 volumes of cold ethanol to the sample.
Add 1 ul of 20 mg/ml glycogen as carrier.
Freeze the mixture for at least 30 minutes at -80°C.
Centrifuge at 13,200 rpm for 20 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 1 ml of 70% ethanol, centrifuge at 13,200 rpm for 5 minutes at room temperature, then discard the supernatant.
Air-dry the pellet and resuspend in an appropriate volume of water or buffer.
Use DEPC nuclease-free H2O to dilute eluate for qPCR analysis.
Store diluted eluate in small aliquots at -20°C, avoiding freeze-thaw cycles.
Perform qPCR using SYBR Green and standard settings on a real-time PCR instrument.
Measure immunoprecipitated DNA samples alongside serial dilutions of input DNA.
Express the amount of DNA in immunoprecipitated material as a percentage of input material for each antibody.
